summary: Summit near Smithers where ten men were to build a lookout in 1939; today hikers find a communication tower and picnic table on top.

access.note: Walkers reach the summit on foot. The trail crosses three gates on private property, and trail guides ask hikers to use the foot gates and close the gates behind them.

visit.trail_note: Easy walk through aspen forest and meadows, starting about ten minutes northeast of Smithers. A bear warning was in place at the trailhead.

events.note: Canada Lookouts quotes a June 1939 Province item saying a lookout would be built at Malkow. Planned work, not a finished tower.

notes_for_editor: The only history is the June 1939 Province item, quoted by Canada Lookouts, and it describes planned work; no source confirms that a lookout was finished, who built it, its design, or whether any cab survives. The Province item puts the work in the Prince Rupert district, a forest district name the sources do not map onto today's Bulkley-Nechako. Trailpeak's page is undated; the Spirko hike report (dated August 7, 2026) is the only dated observation of the summit, and it mentions buildings and trees on top. The access level public is an inference from two trail guides that describe the walk and its gates on private land; the land status is not stated. Kind, agency and status remain unknown and are not recorded in facts.
